message:
Command `cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/hiredis && cat > /workspace/candidate_trace.json <<'JSON'
[
  {"step":1,"file":"fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":34,"var":"data/size","code":"if (size < 1) return 0;","note":"Attacker-controlled bytes are accepted as long as the input is non-empty, so the first byte can drive the format string path."},
  {"step":2,"file":"fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":37,"var":"new_str","code":"new_str = malloc(size+1);","note":"The raw input is copied into a heap buffer and NUL-terminated, making it a C string used as the format argument."},
  {"step":3,"file":"fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":40,"var":"new_str","code":"memcpy(new_str, data, size); new_str[size] = '\\0';","note":"The attacker controls the exact format string contents passed to redisFormatCommand()."},
  {"step":4,"file":"fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":42,"var":"new_str","code":"redisFormatCommand(&cmd, new_str);","note":"The untrusted string is interpreted as a printf-like Redis command format, so malformed specifiers can make the formatter fail."},
  {"step":5,"file":"hiredis.c","function":"redisFormatCommand","line":549,"var":"len","code":"len = redisvFormatCommand(target,format,ap);","note":"redisFormatCommand() forwards the attacker-controlled format to the variadic formatter and receives its status code."},
  {"step":6,"file":"hiredis.c","function":"redisFormatCommand","line":555,"var":"len","code":"if (len < 0) len = -1;","note":"Any formatter failure is normalized to -1, but the callee may already have allocated output memory before returning the error."},
  {"step":7,"file":"hiredis.c","function":"redisvFormatCommand","line":null,"var":"cmd/target","code":"Formatter allocates the command buffer while parsing the format string, then returns an error for invalid or incomplete directives.","note":"This is the root cause: allocation happens on the failure path, so a bad format can leave a heap allocation reachable only through the caller's output pointer."},
  {"step":8,"file":"fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":44,"var":"cmd","code":"if (cmd != NULL) hi_free(cmd);","note":"The fuzzer only frees successful outputs; on failure it does not observe or clean up any allocation performed before the error return, exposing the leak/crash candidate."}
]
JSON
printf '%%q' 'A' > /workspace/poc1
bash /workspace/submit.sh /workspace/poc1 /workspace/candidate_trace.json || true` executed with exit code 0.
